data.description: Elevation allows elements to be lifted from the background. It can be defined by applying drop shadows or other visual cues, such as color and borders

shadows.description: Elevation using shadows reflects a spatial relationship by indicating separation from the background or allowing content to be scrolled under another element.

levels.name: Elevation Level 0 (Border Inset)
levels.description: 1px inset border shadow using #DDDDDD. Creates a subtle inner border effect for flat elements that need definition without appearing raised.

levels.name: Tertiary Elevation
levels.description: 18% opacity black / Blur: 4px / Y-offset: 2px. Subtle shadow for minimal lift.

levels.name: Secondary Elevation
levels.description: 12% opacity black / Blur: 16px / Y-offset: 6px. Medium elevation for interactive elements.

levels.name: High Elevation
levels.description: 28% opacity black / Blur: 28px / Y-offset: 8px. Strong elevation for prominent floating elements.

levels.name: Primary Elevation
levels.description: 20% opacity black / Blur: 20px / Y-offset: 6px. Standard elevated shadow for cards and panels.

levels.name: Focus Ring (Composite)
levels.description: Complex composite shadow for focus states: 4% opacity subtle shadow, 20% primary elevation, plus 2px white and 4px dark focus rings.
